The child substantially elaborates this same sequence. C02 and C08 share retirement or departure-letter conventions, but neither matches the recipient, occasion, and progression as specifically as C09.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Dear Mr. Justice: It is with great regret that I have read your notice of retirement on Monday, October 13, 1958, as an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.","parent_excerpt":"Dear Mr. Justice: Thank you very much for giving me timely notice that, because of your health, you will retire on October fifteenth.","explanation":"Both use the identical judicial salutation and immediately acknowledge notice of retirement on a specified October date."},{"child_excerpt":"Your work on the Supreme Court was, of course, but a continuation of your earlier years of devoted and dedicated public service. Our country is indebted to you.","parent_excerpt":"May I be permitted to express my appreciation of the many years you have given to public service on the Federal Bench, culminating in your service on the Supreme Court?","explanation":"Both characterize Supreme Court service as the culmination or continuation of a longer record of public service."},{"child_excerpt":"I trust that with the leisure your retirement will bring, your health will greatly improve.","parent_excerpt":"I trust you will find your life in retirement to be filled both with contentment and good health.","explanation":"The closing health wish is expressed through a closely parallel 'I trust' formulation explicitly tied to retirement."}]}
